Police Scam

By: Graham Coetzer | Commission

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
It's a scam with a dramatic sense of theatre - victims are convinced they face imminent arrest by supposed police who've contacted them on video calls - only to be left traumatised and out of pocket

Unique Selling Point:
Our research shows that the "video call scam" has seen a huge increase over the past few months. The scammers M.O. is simple but elaborately planned and executed. Victims receive a phone call from a so called "customs" officer. He tells them a package with their name on has been intercepted at one of our airports. The package contains drugs and fake passports. The victim has to send their details to a WhatsApp nr to clear their name. Once they've done that, they receive a video call from another scammer, dressed in a police uniform. For the next two hours they are threatened with arrest, sent fake asset forfeiture documents and warrants, told they're part of a human trafficking and money laundering operation, and convinced the police are going to arrest them for a crime they did not commit...

Summary:
Once the "policeman" has done his part, the victims are handed over to a so-called "prosecutor", often a female scammer. The prosecutor tells victims they can be let off the hook, if they help the police to catch the money launderers. In order to do so, victims have to pay over large amounts of money into a "special investigation" account. The so called police tell the victims they will use the money transfer to monitor the "money launderers" after which the victims will receive their funds back. Once the scammers have your money, R250 000 in one case, they of course disappear into the shadows.

Further information:
We are investigating all leads on the scammers. One of them may be a correctional services employee.
The bank accounts and SIM cards used in the scam are almost all registered under fake/stolen identities and closed soon after the success of the scam.
This story has not really been covered in the mainstream media yet.
We will shoot dramatisations of the scam and take viewers through he process step by step
We will dramatise our search and investigation
It is nearly impossible to recover funds, or catch the people behind these scams - they are essentially cyber criminals.
We have screen grabs of some of the actual scammers

Police Scammers 6701
24 April 2025
First Draft Script

On Screen Title
Old tricks, rebooted.

Ups Govan
This is the fake police officer, ja? He’s the constable.

Ups “Frank”
Immediately I saw this picture of a police person.

Ups fake cop
You are in big trouble.

Voice
It’s a scam so intricate, it had our team calling on years of investigative experience to make sense of it all.

Ups Graham and Laura
Graham: It must be scary.

Laura: And what it plays into as well is the fact that you don’t trust the police.

Ups Mike
It was a warrant for seizure of my assets. Now that’s scary.

Ups Govan
It’s almost like I’m watching a magic show.

VO:
Impressed by the scammers’ ingenuity…

Ups Chad
Do you know how difficult it is for a victim to open a case at a police station in respect of these types of crimes?

VO:
…we had to remind ourselves of the trauma inflicted by their methods.

Ups Mike
Your credentials have been used in connection with human trafficking and money laundering.


Link Govan
Police impersonations are a familiar threat, often orchestrated by sophisticated syndicates. But in a surprising new twist, the scammers have taken the deception to the next level. Creating a disturbing sense of theatre that’s causing panic and confusion.

Voice
It’s a deception targeting ordinary people.

Ups Mike
I get deliveries now and then, you know that’s why I answer numbers that I don’t know.

Voice
The scam begins with a cellphone call, as it did for retired businessman Mike Combrink.

Ups Mike
Mike: And just a friendly sounding guy said to me that I’m shipping with my ID number. Checked if this is my ID nr, this is my name.

Govan: And he said he was from?

Mike: Bloemfontein Customs.

Voice
Who knew some of our parcels made their way to us via the capital of the Free State! But while the location of customs house changes, it’s often how the ruse begins: a deception we’ve dubbed the 'Video Call Scam’.

Ups Graham
In one case R250 000.

Voice
The so-called customs official must convince the victims they’ve been connected to a suspicious parcel being shipped overseas.

This man, we’ll call “Frank”, was one of those victims and got a similar call a few weeks ago. He’s asked us not to identify him.

Ups “Frank”
It was a guy that introduced himself from Cape Town International Airport Customs Department.

Ups Fake Customs Official
Hello sir, I’m from customs. We’ve intercepted a package with your name on it.

Ups Mike
I’m shipping a package to Mumbai containing a bunch of fake passports, a bunch of bank cards, and 120 grams of MDMA.


Voice
MDMA is in the popular party drug, Ecstacy.

Ups Fake Customs Official
Hey these things will put you away for a very long time.

Voice
That’s true – a VERY long time. If of course, the allegations were accurate, and the so-called customs officials weren’t criminals playing dress up. But so authentic was their planning, that they had the victims’ names and ID numbers and even volunteered their own personal details – at least, the made-up ones.

Ups “Frank”
Frank: There’s obviously a criminal case that’s been opened up, and I need just take down his name, his number, his employee number, the case number, the parcel number, so he gave me all this information.

Govan: How did you react to hearing that a parcel was being sent under your name and ID nr?

Frank: No, I was shocked immediately. You know how could this be, I need to clear my name.

Ups Govan
With hindsight, it’s easy to poke holes into it, because you know that it’s fake. But in the moment…

Ups Laura: Well we’re not under pressure right now, you know.

Voice
Part 1 of the scam ramps up the psychological pressure on the victims.

Ups Chad Thomas
They’re finding victims that they know will be afraid of the police. So it’s normally middle-aged people, people who are slightly older, people who are afraid of the system.

Voice
As a financial crime investigator, Chad Thomas, has seen it all. But even he’s taken aback by the intricacy of this scam.

Ups Chad Thomas
They’ve heard things that are horror stories, you get raped in the cells, you get assaulted, you could get murdered. The Numbers gang will keep you hostage.

Voice
The fake-but-believable customs guy then tells the victims the police will be in touch. It’s time for part 2 of the scam.

Ups “Frank”
And the next moment there was an incoming call, a video call, on whatsapp.

Voice
It’s from a man dressed in police uniform claiming to be a constable.

Ups Fake Cop
Ok sir, I’m going to help you open a case for the use of your ID and your name.


Ups Frank
And he sat in front of a notice board that typically looked like the notice boards that you’ll find in a police station.

Voice
According to his whatsapp profile he was Constable David Mothapo from Greenpoint police station. This is a picture of him Frank was able to take while they were talking.

Ups Govan
So this would be the fake cops.

Voice
The grainy video, realistic background and fake uniform make it all seem chillingly authentic.

Link Govan
Imagine trying to catch a shadow. These cybercriminals are almost impossible to trace. They use unregistered sim cards to call from, and open bank accounts using fake identities.

Voice
And, while Green Point in Cape Town offers a range of services to its residents, a police station isn’t one of them. Even that was a lie.

Govan and Laura
Laura: So there were five numbers, two of them were unregistered, of the others one guy is deceased…

Voice
Tracing the cell phone numbers leads nowhere as they’re either stolen or fake.

The victims, meanwhile, are lured even deeper into the trap.

Ups Mike
So he says but he’s just going to check if my ID nr has been used for any other fraud, any other crimes.

Voice
And this signals the start of the scam’s most audacious twist: the fake Constable then radios his fake headquarters to speak to a fake colleague. All while STILL on the call.

Ups “Frank”
Frank: And then he spoke over a two-way radio.

Govan: A “walkie talkie?”

Frank: Ja, ja, ja. And he called the guy on the radio, and he responded, and he said I need you to look into this ID number.

Ups Fake Police officer
Alpha, come in this is six.

Ups Mike
Mike: He called about four times, and then he apologised, he said they are very busy.

Ups “Frank”
And then all of a sudden the voice came back and he said listen you need to arrest this guy immediately. There’s a warrant out for his arrest.

Ups Mike
Human trafficking and money laundering.

Ups Fake Police officer
Do you know how serious human trafficking and money laundering charges are?

Link Govan
At their core these scams follow a familiar playbook. The scammers create a sense of urgency by escalating fear with threats of imminent arrest.

Ups Chad
It’s scam 101. You know why we call them con artists? Because they’re confident and convincing.

Voice
But the success of the video call scam hinges on the victims being fearful of arrest. And to ensure that happens, the scammers need authentic looking documents.

Ups Mike
And then he sent me the warrants.

Voice
Both Mike and Frank were WhatsApped fake arrest warrants and asset seizure orders. To persuade them not to contact the real authorities, they were even sent documents like this one, warning them they were part of a sensitive investigation.

Ups “Frank”
This is a matter of state security or something.

Ups Mike
Mike: Some fine and three years in prison if I talk.

Upsound Govan and Laura
Govan: Ok, I mean when you put it up, side by side then…

Laura: It’s so obvious.

Voice
The warrant is obviously fake when compared to the real thing, but to the uninitiated, it looks convincing.

Ups Graham
Under the criminal procedure act hey…

Ups Laura
Ja.

Ups Graham
…which this fake one doesn’t make any mention of. Another interesting thing is our real… all the SAPS documents usually are stamped with the squares, I never see round…

Ups Laura
Oh, round stamps.

Ups Graham
… stamps.

Voice
In most cases it takes close to an hour for the scammers to finally cut to the chase. Until then, there’s no talk of money changing hands.

Ups Mike
There was no hint that he’s lying, or that he’s putting up a show or anything like that.

Voice
The perfect time for the third and final part of the scam – enter, the prosecutor.

Ups “Frank”
And she was sitting in an office with two flags on both sides of her. The one was the country’s flag.

Ups Fake Prosecutor
So the charges against you are very serious, and if you don’t cooperate then you will be arrested.

Voice
Also referred to as the chief and often portrayed by a female, the prosecutor’s job is to offer the victims a way out – if they cooperate.

Ups “Frank”
Frank: She proceeded to say that their audit team is busy, sitting and waiting, and they’re also looking at this interview, and she’s going to ask me about my accounts. She asked me about my personal account, about my business accounts.

Govan: Did you tell her how much was in the account, or did she want proof?

Frank: They asked me, they said I must show them screen shots, on my phone.

Upsound Govan
So, how does the victim end up losing money, are you paying them so that they can make the case go away?

Upsound Graham
So in this case, funnily enough, no. What the scammers are convincing you of is that you are going to be part of this investigation…

Voice
It’s the moment the entire deception has been leading to. Victims are told they must transfer their funds into – wait for it - a “special police account” – supposedly so the authorities can track the real money launderers.

Ups Fake Prosecutor
You will have to transfer all the money that you have into that account.

Ups Mike
Once the investigation is complete, they will refund everything, minus R34.50. Which is some sort of fee, but all other expenses will be borne by the state.

Voice
For Mike, the ruse was finally up.

Ups Mike
They asked for money, the moment they asked for money, that’s the warning sign I’ve been waiting for.

Voice
He ended the call and contacted his lawyer who confirmed the warrant and other documents were fake.

Frank on the other hand was convinced he was helping the police.

Ups Frank
The sooner we can try and track this money, the sooner we can try to get behind what’s happening.

Voice
Frank transferred nearly a quarter of a million rand from his business account in two payments.

Ups “Frank”
She said to me that if you cooperate then this will all go smoothly but if not we are going to have to arrest you.

Voice
Adding insult to injury, the scammers even sent him these certificates after the payments – supposedly clearing him of any crime.

Upsound “Frank”
Govan: Looking at it now, what do you think?

Frank: You feel like a complete fool afterwards, because you keep telling yourself why didn’t I see that, why didn’t I see that. For me the fear throughout this process was that myself or my family will be jeopardized in any way, and I think that was also the reason why I kept working with them.

Voice
By the time the bank froze the account Frank had paid into, his money had already been withdrawn at various ATM’s.

Syndicates use fake ID’s or “money mules” – people willing to open bank accounts in return for payments – to get away with the cash. Another dead end for investigators.

Ups Chad
They get taken to banks to open accounts, they then hand over their bank card, they hand over their pin, they hand over all their particulars. So when the police follow up the lead, it lands up with a mule. And that mule doesn’t know what the syndicate has done, and doesn’t in fact know who the syndicate is, because they were dealing with a runner.

Voice
But very few cases will ever be investigated to that extent.

Ups Chad
Remember with our high rates of crime and the multitude of organised crime syndicates operating in South Africa, our specialised investigators within the Hawks and within the police, are having to concentrate on matters that exceed a couple of million rand.

Voice
Frank also snuck this picture of another fake police officer who made a cameo appearance in his video call—but, after alerting the “not-fake police” and other authorities, he doesn’t expect his case to go anywhere.

Ups Govan
Constable David Mothapo still has a SAPS logo as his whatsapp profile picture. I’ll just video call him. See if he picks up.

Ringing
So it’s just calling, it’s not ringing, which means that the number isn’t connected to data.

Voice
The number has likely been discarded.

Ups Mike
I mean what’s more scary to me, is that I don’t want to go report this to the police, because I don’t trust the police.

Voice
Although, when they phone you out of the blue, that’s arguably the advice even the real police would give.



















PROMOS
Promo 1

Voice
It’s a sophisticated new scam…

Upsound Fake Customs
We’ve intercepted a package with your name on it.

Upsound Mike:
Govan: And he said he was from?

Mike: Bloemfontein customs.

Voice
Police impersonators are video calling innocent members of the public in a con with a touch of theatre.

Ups Mike
human trafficking and money laundering.




Promo 2

Voice
They’re told to cooperate or face the consequences…

Upsound Mike
three years in prison if I talk.

Voice
Part crime, part performance, it’s a police impersonation scam with a new twist. And it’s fooling people fast.

Ups “Frank”
Govan: Did you tell her how much was in the account?

Frank: they said I must show them screen shots, on my phone.


Promo 3

Voice
Imagine receiving a video call from a police officer accusing you of being involved in serious crimes.

Ups Mike
human trafficking and money laundering.

Voice
A new scam has hit our streets, and the syndicates running it are raking in the cash.

Ups “Frank”
She said to me that if you cooperate then this will all go smoothly but if not then we are going to have to arrest you.

Ups Govan With hindsight, it’s easy to poke holes into it, because you know that it’s fake. But in the moment… Ups Laura: Well we’re not under pressure right now, you know. Voice Part 1 of the scam ramps up the psychological pressure on the victims. Ups Chad Thomas They’re finding victims that they know will be afraid of the police. So it’s normally middle-aged people, people who are slightly older, people who are afraid of the system. Voice As a financial crime investigator, Chad Thomas, has seen it all. But even he’s taken aback by the intricacy of this scam. Ups Chad Thomas They’ve heard things that are horror stories, you get raped in the cells, you get assaulted, you could get murdered. The Numbers gang will keep you hostage. Voice The fake-but-believable customs guy then tells the victims the police will be in touch. It’s time for part 2 of the scam. Ups “Frank” And the next moment there was an incoming call, a video call, on whatsapp. Voice It’s from a man dressed in police uniform claiming to be a constable. Ups Fake Cop Ok sir, I’m going to help you open a case for the use of your ID and your name. Ups Frank And he sat in front of a notice board that typically looked like the notice boards that you’ll find in a police station. Voice According to his whatsapp profile he was Constable David Mothapo from Greenpoint police station. This is a picture of him Frank was able to take while they were talking. Ups Govan So this would be the fake cops. Voice The grainy video, realistic background and fake uniform make it all seem chillingly authentic. Link Govan Imagine trying to catch a shadow. These cybercriminals are almost impossible to trace. They use unregistered sim cards to call from, and open bank accounts using fake identities. Voice And, while Green Point in Cape Town offers a range of services to its residents, a police station isn’t one of them. Even that was a lie. Govan and Laura Laura: So there were five numbers, two of them were unregistered, of the others one guy is deceased… Voice Tracing the cell phone numbers leads nowhere as they’re either stolen or fake. The victims, meanwhile, are lured even deeper into the trap. Ups Mike So he says but he’s just going to check if my ID nr has been used for any other fraud, any other crimes. Voice And this signals the start of the scam’s most audacious twist: the fake Constable then radios his fake headquarters to speak to a fake colleague. All while STILL on the call. Ups “Frank” Frank: And then he spoke over a two-way radio. Govan: A “walkie talkie?” Frank: Ja, ja, ja. And he called the guy on the radio, and he responded, and he said I need you to look into this ID number. Ups Fake Police officer Alpha, come in this is six. Ups Mike Mike: He called about four times, and then he apologised, he said they are very busy. Ups “Frank” And then all of a sudden the voice came back and he said listen you need to arrest this guy immediately. There’s a warrant out for his arrest. Ups Mike Human trafficking and money laundering. Ups Fake Police officer Do you know how serious human trafficking and money laundering charges are? Link Govan At their core these scams follow a familiar playbook. The scammers create a sense of urgency by escalating fear with threats of imminent arrest. Ups Chad It’s scam 101. You know why we call them con artists? Because they’re confident and convincing. Voice But the success of the video call scam hinges on the victims being fearful of arrest. And to ensure that happens, the scammers need authentic looking documents. Ups Mike And then he sent me the warrants. Voice Both Mike and Frank were WhatsApped fake arrest warrants and asset seizure orders. To persuade them not to contact the real authorities, they were even sent documents like this one, warning them they were part of a sensitive investigation. Ups “Frank” This is a matter of state security or something. Ups Mike Mike: Some fine and three years in prison if I talk. Upsound Govan and Laura Govan: Ok, I mean when you put it up, side by side then… Laura: It’s so obvious. Voice The warrant is obviously fake when compared to the real thing, but to the uninitiated, it looks convincing. Ups Graham Under the criminal procedure act hey… Ups Laura Ja. Ups Graham …which this fake one doesn’t make any mention of. Another interesting thing is our real… all the SAPS documents usually are stamped with the squares, I never see round… Ups Laura Oh, round stamps. Ups Graham … stamps. Voice In most cases it takes close to an hour for the scammers to finally cut to the chase. Until then, there’s no talk of money changing hands. Ups Mike There was no hint that he’s lying, or that he’s putting up a show or anything like that. Voice The perfect time for the third and final part of the scam – enter, the prosecutor. Ups “Frank” And she was sitting in an office with two flags on both sides of her. The one was the country’s flag. Ups Fake Prosecutor So the charges against you are very serious, and if you don’t cooperate then you will be arrested. Voice Also referred to as the chief and often portrayed by a female, the prosecutor’s job is to offer the victims a way out – if they cooperate. Ups “Frank” Frank: She proceeded to say that their audit team is busy, sitting and waiting, and they’re also looking at this interview, and she’s going to ask me about my accounts. She asked me about my personal account, about my business accounts. Govan: Did you tell her how much was in the account, or did she want proof? Frank: They asked me, they said I must show them screen shots, on my phone. Upsound Govan So, how does the victim end up losing money, are you paying them so that they can make the case go away? Upsound Graham So in this case, funnily enough, no. What the scammers are convincing you of is that you are going to be part of this investigation… Voice It’s the moment the entire deception has been leading to. Victims are told they must transfer their funds into – wait for it - a “special police account” – supposedly so the authorities can track the real money launderers. Ups Fake Prosecutor You will have to transfer all the money that you have into that account. Ups Mike Once the investigation is complete, they will refund everything, minus R34.50. Which is some sort of fee, but all other expenses will be borne by the state. Voice For Mike, the ruse was finally up. Ups Mike They asked for money, the moment they asked for money, that’s the warning sign I’ve been waiting for. Voice He ended the call and contacted his lawyer who confirmed the warrant and other documents were fake. Frank on the other hand was convinced he was helping the police. Ups Frank The sooner we can try and track this money, the sooner we can try to get behind what’s happening. Voice Frank transferred nearly a quarter of a million rand from his business account in two payments. Ups “Frank” She said to me that if you cooperate then this will all go smoothly but if not we are going to have to arrest you. Voice Adding insult to injury, the scammers even sent him these certificates after the payments – supposedly clearing him of any crime. Upsound “Frank” Govan: Looking at it now, what do you think? Frank: You feel like a complete fool afterwards, because you keep telling yourself why didn’t I see that, why didn’t I see that. For me the fear throughout this process was that myself or my family will be jeopardized in any way, and I think that was also the reason why I kept working with them. Voice By the time the bank froze the account Frank had paid into, his money had already been withdrawn at various ATM’s. Syndicates use fake ID’s or “money mules” – people willing to open bank accounts in return for payments – to get away with the cash. Another dead end for investigators. Ups Chad They get taken to banks to open accounts, they then hand over their bank card, they hand over their pin, they hand over all their particulars. So when the police follow up the lead, it lands up with a mule. And that mule doesn’t know what the syndicate has done, and doesn’t in fact know who the syndicate is, because they were dealing with a runner. Voice But very few cases will ever be investigated to that extent. Ups Chad Remember with our high rates of crime and the multitude of organised crime syndicates operating in South Africa, our specialised investigators within the Hawks and within the police, are having to concentrate on matters that exceed a couple of million rand. Voice Frank also snuck this picture of another fake police officer who made a cameo appearance in his video call—but, after alerting the “not-fake police” and other authorities, he doesn’t expect his case to go anywhere. Ups Govan Constable David Mothapo still has a SAPS logo as his whatsapp profile picture. I’ll just video call him. See if he picks up. Ringing So it’s just calling, it’s not ringing, which means that the number isn’t connected to data. Voice The number has likely been discarded. Ups Mike I mean what’s more scary to me, is that I don’t want to go report this to the police, because I don’t trust the police. Voice Although, when they phone you out of the blue, that’s arguably the advice even the real police would give. PROMOS Promo 1 Voice It’s a sophisticated new scam… Upsound Fake Customs We’ve intercepted a package with your name on it. Upsound Mike: Govan: And he said he was from? Mike: Bloemfontein customs. Voice Police impersonators are video calling innocent members of the public in a con with a touch of theatre. Ups Mike human trafficking and money laundering. Promo 2 Voice They’re told to cooperate or face the consequences… Upsound Mike three years in prison if I talk. Voice Part crime, part performance, it’s a police impersonation scam with a new twist. And it’s fooling people fast. Ups “Frank” Govan: Did you tell her how much was in the account? Frank: they said I must show them screen shots, on my phone. Promo 3 Voice Imagine receiving a video call from a police officer accusing you of being involved in serious crimes. Ups Mike human trafficking and money laundering. Voice A new scam has hit our streets, and the syndicates running it are raking in the cash. Ups “Frank” She said to me that if you cooperate then this will all go smoothly but if not then we are going to have to arrest you.

metadata.One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...): It's a scam with a dramatic sense of theatre - victims are convinced they face imminent arrest by supposed police who've contacted them on video calls - only to be left traumatised and out of pocket
metadata.Unique Selling Point: Our research shows that the "video call scam" has seen a huge increase over the past few months. The scammers M.O. is simple but elaborately planned and executed. Victims receive a phone call from a so called "customs" officer. He tells them a package with their name on has been intercepted at one of our airports. The package contains drugs and fake passports. The victim has to send their details to a WhatsApp nr to clear their name. Once they've done that, they receive a video call from another scammer, dressed in a police uniform. For the next two hours they are threatened with arrest, sent fake asset forfeiture documents and warrants, told they're part of a human trafficking and money laundering operation, and convinced the police are going to arrest them for a crime they did not commit...
metadata.Summary: Once the "policeman" has done his part, the victims are handed over to a so-called "prosecutor", often a female scammer. The prosecutor tells victims they can be let off the hook, if they help the police to catch the money launderers. In order to do so, victims have to pay over large amounts of money into a "special investigation" account. The so called police tell the victims they will use the money transfer to monitor the "money launderers" after which the victims will receive their funds back. Once the scammers have your money, R250 000 in one case, they of course disappear into the shadows.
metadata.Further information: We are investigating all leads on the scammers. One of them may be a correctional services employee. The bank accounts and SIM cards used in the scam are almost all registered under fake/stolen identities and closed soon after the success of the scam. This story has not really been covered in the mainstream media yet. We will shoot dramatisations of the scam and take viewers through he process step by step We will dramatise our search and investigation It is nearly impossible to recover funds, or catch the people behind these scams - they are essentially cyber criminals. We have screen grabs of some of the actual scammers
